A.biggest_strength: Broad interactive language coverage spanning 13 languages plus x86-64 assembly in the stepper, accompanied by detailed calling convention breakdowns and comparison tables.
A.biggest_weakness: The stack visualization is relatively static and text-heavy, showing frames and variable updates as text labels rather than animating the actual transfer of arguments and return value substitution.

B.biggest_strength: Exceptional visual explanation and system depth: arguments physically fly into parameter slots, return values substitute in-place into waiting caller expressions, and real-world compiler bytecodes and empirical stack limits are interactively demonstrated.
B.biggest_weakness: The interactive animation only supports 6 languages (Python, JavaScript, Ruby, C, Java, Rust), leaving the remaining 7 languages to the reference table below.

structured_output.reasons: Page B is the overall winner because it truly visualizes the physical mechanisms of a function call rather than just presenting text alongside boxes. Its animated dataflow shows argument chips landing in parameter slots and return values substituting into expressions within waiting caller frames. Furthermore, B provides extraordinary engineering depth by displaying real bytecode/disassembly for 6 runtime models and empirical stack-size measurements, paired with superior visual craft, full keyboard navigation, robust reduced-motion support, and adaptive mobile formatting. While Page A offers broader interactive language coverage (13 languages vs B's 6), B is a significantly more memorable, instructive, and technically rigorous explainer.
